shot-ren-lane.mp4.generated_with: seedance_2_0 with the character's locked element, 6s, 1920x1080, silent
shot-ren-lane.mp4.note: Ren in the UNDERWATER STREAMLINE PHASE off the start - the fastest phase of any race and, per the swim codex, the show's single best-integrated rule-as-story-beat. Body one rigid line, arms locked overhead, head buried between the biceps with only goggles and jaw showing, dolphin kick from the chest through pointed toes. Precision as menace: he is not stroking, he is a shape moving through water. Legal textile jammers, waist to above the knee.
shot-ren-lane.mp4.verification: SUPERSEDES a shot that showed a freestyle arm recovery UNDERWATER with the head raised looking forward - two errors a swimmer catches in the first second, neither caught by the art gate because it checked identity only. Took three passes. Pass 1 fixed the recovery but left the swimmer small in frame; pass 2 was closer but the hands were apart, which is a 'superman glide', not a streamline. Pass 3 succeeded by describing the SILHOUETTE rather than the anatomy: in a strict side profile a correct streamline shows only ONE arm and ONE hand, because the far ones occlude completely. Verified across 6 sampled frames: single-blade silhouette held, head buried, lane lines correctly ABOVE him, jammers legal. FOURTH PASS fixed the legs, on a creator note that still-frame review could never have produced: the dolphin kick undulation initiates at the CHEST, not the legs, and travels chest to hips to knees to feet like a crack running down a whip. Legs now joined as one tail throughout, and the wave visibly leads from the body rather than the feet flapping. Creator confirmed this take as the correct movement. 1280x720 from the model, upscaled to 1920x1080 (Topaz) and transcoded to h264 to match the cut.

shot-kemar-joy.mp4.generated_with: seedance_2_0 with the character's locked element, 6s 720p, upscaled to 1920x1080 by Topaz (job 25cec8ff-6bac-4bbd-9b13-37bc99c14074) and transcoded to h264, silent
shot-kemar-joy.mp4.note: Kemar swimming real SURFACE freestyle, shot SPLIT-LEVEL with the lens at the waterline. THE BODY LINE IS THE POINT: head, shoulders, hips and heels sit at ONE depth, forming a single straight line parallel to the pool floor, held for the whole 6.04s. The neck is neutral - the head is a continuation of the spine with no angle at the shoulders - which is what fixes the two notes that read as separate faults but are the same fault: a craned neck and sagging hips. He is IN the water and not on it: the waterline crosses the crown, the back and hips are submerged, and the only things breaking the surface are the rolling shoulder and the recovering arm. Verified across a full-clip frame walk at 8fps that the recovering arm genuinely clears the surface and swings forward through AIR, water sheeting off the fingers - the fault this shot existed to fix was arm recovery underwater, so that is checked as a sequence and not from a single frame. Fourth and final take; the three before it each broke something else while fixing the line.
shot-kemar-joy.mp4.verification: Took five passes, and each note came from the creator rather than from the gate, because the gate could only check identity. Pass 1-2: the original shot had a freestyle arm recovery UNDERWATER with the head raised - two errors a swimmer catches in the first second. Pass 3 moved him to the surface and fixed both, which also improved the staging: Ren now owns the silent submerged line and Kemar owns the breathing sunlit one. Pass 4 fixed a face that read androgynous in the breathing frame, by restating age and sex structurally (jawline, brow, neck, shoulders) rather than as a pronoun; the rejected sibling take from that same pass fixed the face but over-rotated the head so both goggles cleared the water, and added a flag-like graphic to the wrap. Pass 5 fixed the body riding too high - the last and most persistent error, and one the codex had no rule for until now. Creator picked this take over a fully-underwater alternative because that one, while prettier, duplicated Ren's submerged beat. 1280x720 upscaled to 1920x1080 (Topaz), transcoded to h264, 6.04s - same as the shot it replaces, so no cut point moved. TRIMMED to 4.21s. The 6.04s clip drifted WITHIN itself: for the first 4.2 seconds the camera holds split-level with the body correctly submerged, then at about 4.3s it lifts above the waterline, the swimmer rides on top with a shadow beneath, and the face changes enough to read as a different person. Creator caught it as 'looks like two different people' - which is the same defect as 'sitting too high', not a separate one. The break was bracketed to between 4.2s and 4.4s by frame sampling and the clip cut at the last verified-good frame. Consistency re-verified across 8 frames of the trimmed shot.

undertow-theme.wav.generated_with: composed in code by build-score.py - additive/subtractive synthesis in numpy, zero generated audio, zero library music
undertow-theme.wav.note: "Deep Calls to Deep" - the main theme, 64s concert statement. D minor, 60 BPM (a resting heart rate; one beat = one second of breath-hold). The grammar is the series' own title phrase from Psalm 42:7 made literal: THE CALL, a five-note figure that falls a sixth then lifts one step, is answered by THE SAME FIGURE from below - an octave and a fifth down, two bars late, slower and heavier. That is dramatically loadable: an answer arriving EARLY is the deep reaching for someone, an answer in the WRONG key is the Second Tide, an answer that never comes is the worst thing in the show. Voices: struck-glass bowls with inharmonic partials (the call), sub sine (the answer), a detuned pad breathing on a 12s cycle (the sea), and a nyabinghi-rooted heartbeat pulse. Owned outright - no licence attached to the thing the series is identified by.
undertow-theme.wav.verification: -16.0 LUFS, -1.5 dBTP, stereo correlation +0.85, DC 0.000000, no energy below 22Hz, starts and ends at silence. Spectrogram read. Four engineering defects were found and fixed before this master: the file was dual-mono (L and R bit-identical); the reverb sat ~22dB below what its mix parameter claimed, so a score about underwater space had almost none; the ANSWER masked the CALL by 11dB RMS (low stem 89% of mix energy against lead at 7.2%); and the glass voice decayed its upper partials fastest, which is a drum not a bowl, leaving under 1% of energy above 400Hz for EQ to work with. The last was fixed in the instrument, not the equaliser - EQ cannot lift content that was never synthesised.
undertow-theme.wav.engineering: 24-bit/48kHz stereo, -16.0 LUFS integrated, true peak under -1.0 dBTP (measured 4x oversampled per ITU-R BS.1770). Mastered through the shared chain in mastering.py: DC block, 24Hz subsonic filter, stereo placement, 120Hz bass mono-maker, loudness trim, look-ahead channel-linked true-peak limiter, endpoint seal. Verified by qc/verify_mastering.py.

signatures/fathom-sunlit.wav.note: Fathom rank stinger: SUNLIT (D5). 0-20m. Awakened novice; most club swimmers cap here. Bright and close. Full attack, shortest tail. The five ranks spell the show's home chord downward - D5 A4 F4 D3 D2 - so the ladder is the theme. Two things change together as you descend, both physically true of water: high frequency dies and reverb grows. Nobody has to be told which is deeper.
